title: Lower a loaded steel hotel pan level into a steam-table well and let go
instruction: Move the full steel pan from the table into the black steam-table well and let go, so it sits in the well with its flange resting on the counter.
context: Restaurant cooks (O*NET 35-2014.00, about 1.4 million US workers per BLS) and food preparation workers (35-2021.00, about 0.9 million) set full hot pans into steam-table wells several times every service. A half-size pan of 2.4 to 3 kg of liquid food spills scalding liquid if it is tilted, and jams on the well edge or drops if it is not aligned. Unlike the dock-a-laptop and tart-ring lowering tasks, the load is a heavy open vessel with a geometric spill limit and a 6 mm-per-side fit.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left, table top 74.75 cm). Steel pan: floor 32.5 x 26.5 cm, 40 mm deep, walls 2 mm, flange 1 cm wide and 3 mm thick (outside 34.5 x 28.5 cm), with an orange upright tab 2.4 x 2 x 4.5 cm on the flange at each short end (y +-16.75), friction 0.5, 2.4 kg in total: pan about 0.7 kg plus 20 mm of cold tap water (1.68 kg, drawn as a fused blue box), long axis along y, start centre x 8.5, y 0. Black steam-table counter: four fixed strips 4 cm high around a pit 27.7 (x) x 33.7 (y) cm, centre x 40, y 0; strips 3 cm wide at the x ends and 4.5 cm wide at the y sides.
scoring: Scored on the end pose with a 1 s hold. 0 if at any step the 20 mm of water would overflow the pan at its lowest rim corner (corner drop 0.1325 m x |n_x/n_z| + 0.1625 m x |n_y/n_z| above the 17 mm freeboard; alone 7.3 degrees across the 265 mm width or 6.0 degrees along the 325 mm length, less when combined; real test: more than 5 mL collected on a weighed mat or tray), moves faster than 0.5 m/s (dropped), or ends off the table. 0.25 pan held over the well (centre within 20 mm, flange underside 12 mm or more above the counter). 0.5 pan underside below the counter top within 20 mm of the pit centre but the flange not seated. 0.75 all four flange corners within 2 mm of the counter top, centre within 8 mm, tilt at most 2 degrees. 1.0 as 0.75 with both grippers open and 40 mm clear of the handle tabs, pan and arms still, for 20 consecutive steps.
reset_notes: Pan with its water on the table, flange 4 mm from the counter front, long axis along y; counter fixed.
fidelity: Liquid is not simulated: spill = geometric overflow at the lowest rim corner (17 mm freeboard: 7.3 deg across, 6.0 deg along, less combined) for 20 mm of cold water in a 40 mm pan; no slosh. Real test: weighed catch mat, <= 5 mL. Pan is one rigid 2.4 kg body (about 0.7 kg pan + 1.68 kg water). Well = four fixed boxes on the table. Handles are upright tabs. Scorer reads gripper state.
scores: Dream-1 run (scorer v2): 0.0, pan untouched; demo: 1.0 on the final scorer
